account: It is early on Day 1, and I am at the town hall after reading today's appointment book and the secretary's two supporting notes. Today I have office at eight, a mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, tea at the east-bank cottage at three, office again at half past four, and home at seven. The unusual uncertainty is that the mill inspection is scheduled but still not directly confirmed. The secretary visited last evening, found no staff, and could not establish who manages the records: the baker and innkeeper did not know, and Freight had not answered before the secretary left. This does not establish any wrongdoing or grain shortage. The inspection is intended to review grain stocks, deliveries, shortages if any, and storage concerns; no supplies were ordered moved. I should discuss renewed morning contact with the secretary at eight and keep the scheduled inspection unless it is changed. Yesterday's tea was quiet and friendly. I personally established the cottage's location, although the host's name remains unknown to me beyond 'neighbour.' I have no evidence of any other unusual activity in town today.
